feature: Simple text input field — submit & validation
summary: The target page provides a single required text input (id: id_text_string, label: Text string*). Submission is triggered by pressing Enter (no explicit submit button). After a valid non-empty submission the page echoes the submitted value as a visible result. An empty submission is blocked by the browser's native required-field validation, so no success message appears.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Typing text into the input field and submitting displays a success message.
The success message contains or reflects the submitted value.
Submitting with an empty field does not show a success message.
The input field is accessible by label or role.
The form submission mechanism is keyboard accessible.

scenarios.scenario: Page load shows a visible, labeled text input.
steps: Locate the element by role textbox with name 'Text string*'
scenarios.expectedResult: A visible textbox labeled 'Text string*' is present on initial page load.

scenarios.scenario: Submitting a non-empty value echoes it on the page.
steps: Fill the input with a test string
Press Enter to submit the form
Assert the submitted value is visible in the response area
scenarios.expectedResult: The submitted value appears visibly on the page after submission.

scenarios.scenario: Submitting an empty field does not display a success message.
steps: Attempt to submit by pressing Enter
Assert no success/result text is displayed
scenarios.expectedResult: No success message is shown; native required-field validation blocks the submission.

scenarios.scenario: Input is accessible by role and label.
steps: Locate the input via getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Text string*' })
Assert the element is visible and editable
scenarios.expectedResult: The input is reachable and interactable through its ARIA role and associated label.

steps: Assert the submitted value is visible
scenarios.expectedResult: The entire submission flow is completable with keyboard only.

assumptions.assumption: There is no explicit Submit button; the form is submitted by pressing Enter while focused on the input.
The success response echoes the submitted text exactly as entered.

risks.risk: Native browser validation for required fields may behave differently across browser engines.
risks.recommendation: Run tests in Chromium where native constraint validation is consistent.

recommendation.comment: All acceptance criteria are fully covered by the defined scenarios. Page evidence confirms the submission mechanism and success response behaviour.
